channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound: Steady against US Dollar before key BoE and data – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the British Pound (GBP) is consolidating recent gains around 1.3400, with domestic risk elevated ahead of next week’s CPI, labour data and the Bank of England decision.

item.title: Euro supported by hawkish ECB rhetoric as British Pound struggles after weak GDP
item.description: EUR/GBP holds firm on Friday, with the Euro (EUR) modestly outperforming the British Pound (GBP) as weak UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data reinforced signs of a slowing economy. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8633, up from an intraday low of 0.8625.

item.title: CEE FX: Risk-on bounce but policy still key – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes that headlines on a possible end to the US-Iran conflict triggered a risk-on move, helping Central and Eastern European currencies erase recent losses.

item.title: Gold pauses recovery as traders await clarity on US-Iran peace deal
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates on Friday as traders await further developments on a potential US-Iran peace deal. At the time of writing, XAU/USD is trading around $4,189 after climbing to an intraday high of $4,246 earlier in the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Overbought Dollar holds near 1.40 ceiling – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret observe that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is weighed down by weaker Oil prices linked to Iran peace hopes, even as improved risk appetite offers some support.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar dips as robust US sentiment, inflation data underpin US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5830 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day as the US Dollar (USD) maintains a firm tone following a series of strong US economic releases.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish forecasts point to higher terminal rate – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European Economics team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak and colleagues, notes that the ECB delivered a 25bp hike to a 2.25% depo rate and unveiled more hawkish forecasts.

item.title: Bank of England: Hold stance extended as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists expect the Bank of England (BoE) to keep Bank Rate at 3.75% with a 7-2 vote as Greene joins Pill in calling for a hike. They highlight persistent inflation pressures, upside risks from energy and airfare, and softer demand.

item.title: Breaking: United States Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises to 48.9 in June
item.description: Consumer confidence in the United States (US) improved slightly in June, with the University of Michigan's (UoM) Consumer Sentiment Index rising to 48.9 in the flash estimate from 44.8 in May. This print came in better than the market expectation of 46.

item.title: British Pound: Poised to fall toward 1.3100 against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad says GBP/USD has given back part of its US-Iran-related gains and is expected to fall to 1.3100 as United States (US) growth outpaces the United Kingdom (UK).

item.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh policy shift and inflation focus – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategists assess how Kevin Warsh may reshape Federal Reserve (Fed) policy.

item.title: US Dollar: Peace deal talk keeps support intact – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that a potential US-Iran peace deal has softened the Dollar, but DXY is still holding firm. He highlights that energy supply losses and inflation risks persist unless Oil flows freely through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: RSI points lower as prices remain below key SMAs
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) pares some part of earlier losses on Friday as markets seek confirmation of a possible US-Iran agreement, prompting traders to refrain from placing aggressive bearish bets.

item.title: Indian Rupee: External shocks pressure currency outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts Charlie Lay and Moses Lim argue that the Rupee remains vulnerable to external shocks, notably Middle East tensions, higher energy costs and El Nino-related risks.

item.title: Gold: Fed expectations cap upside for now – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Precious Metals, particularly Gold, are struggling to gain traction as elevated Fed hike probabilities keep real rates high. CTA's (Commodity Trading Advisors) are running a small net short and scenario analysis points to a relatively tight trading band.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips as softer Oil, robust US inflation weigh on CAD
item.description: USD/CAD trades higher around 1.3990 on Friday, with the US Dollar (USD) benefiting from stronger-than-expected inflation data in the United States (US), while the Canadian Dollar (CAD) remains weighed down by falling Oil prices and a Bank of Canada (BoC) that is showing little urgency to raise rates

item.title: European Central Bank: Further rate hikes seen despite softer Oil – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan von Gerich highlights that the ECB delivered a widely expected 25bp hike and is likely to continue tightening, with the next move expected in July. He argues that broadening inflation pressures mean lower energy prices alone will not ease ECB concerns.

item.title: Copper: Tariff risks keep spreads elevated – ING
item.description: ING’s Commodities Strategist Ewa Manthey notes that LME copper is trading near record highs, supported by supply tightness, US tariff-driven stockpiling and AI-related power demand. The market is already pricing US tariff risk, with the COMEX-LME spread around $400/t.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Steady outlook faces USMCA risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note Mexico still appears steady even as conditions become more challenging. Inflation has cooled to 3.94% in May, while Banxico has signalled an end to its easing cycle, leading markets to price potential hikes.

item.title: Fed: Warsh era starts with cautious stance and delayed cuts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Bernd Weidensteiner and Christoph Balz argue that Kevin Warsh’s first Federal Reserve meeting is unlikely to deliver an immediate rate cut, given elevated PCE inflation and a still‑solid labor market.

item.title: British Pound: Policy divergence seen weigh against Euro – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global FX Strategy team, including Dominic Bunning and Yusuke Miyairi, argues that a more hawkish ECB path versus the Bank of England should support the Euro against the Pound.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Bulls struggle to breach a previous support near 1.1600
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has given away previous daily gains against the US Dollar (USD) and is trading practically flat, at 1.1575 at the time of writing.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher-for-longer backdrop supports USD – MUFG
item.description: MUFG analysts Lin Li, Michael Wan, Lloyd Chan and Khang Sek Lee argue that firmer US inflation and resilient labour markets underpin a higher-for-longer global rates backdrop, supporting the US Dollar.

item.title: Euro: Seen drifting toward 1.1400 against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad reports that EUR/USD briefly dipped toward 1.1500 after the ECB decision before rebounding on the US-Iran breakthrough. Haddad expects EUR/USD to edge lower and stabilize closer to 1.1400 as US growth outperforms the Eurozone.

item.title: Indian Rupee extends recovery as US-Iran to sign MoU on Sunday
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) rises sharply higher higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair tumbles to near 95.12 on reports that the United States (US) and Iran will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Geneva on Sunday, resulting in a significant decline in oil prices.

item.title: British Pound picks up as Iran peace hopes offset soft UK GDP data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) maintains a moderately positive tone against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as investors’ optimism about a US-Iran peace deal has offset rather uninspiring UK data.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Downside risk against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts reports USD/BRL has been rebounding from an interim low near 4.88 and is approaching the 200-DMA and a descending trend line around 5.25. They stress the need to see if a base and trend reversal can form, with resistance at 5.32/5.34 and downside risk if 4.99 fails.

item.title: IRNA releases key terms under US-Iran MoU
item.description: Iran’s IRNA news agency releases the major terms of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) discussed with the United States (US). Earlier a report from Bloomberg showed that the MoU will be signed in Geneva on Sunday.

item.title: Fed: Warsh debut expected to stay cautious – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan von Gerich expects Kevin Warsh’s first FOMC meeting on 17 June to deliver a more neutral policy stance, with earlier projected rate cuts likely removed from the dot plot and some hike calls appearing.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hikes rates with hawkish tone – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s European economists highlight that the ECB delivered its first rate hike since 2023, lifting the deposit rate to 2.25% and pairing it with hawkish messaging from President Lagarde.
